title: WRC Generations stages
keys: WRC Generations sends neither a stage nor, it seems, its length: a run is matched by its distance to the finish within 1 % of length_m, and by where earlier runs of a stage started when two stages are that close.
notes: WRC Generations (KT Racing / Nacon, Nov 2022): 21 rallies, 165 special stages, no post-launch rallies and no free-roam or Rally Hub location. 13 rallies of the 2022 calendar plus 8 bonus rallies (Argentina, Chile, Germany, Mexico, Sanremo, Corsica, Turkey, Wales). The stages are fictional cut-downs, not copies of the real stages, so real itinerary lengths do not apply and were not used. Stage names follow the in-game spelling from wrcsetups.com and TechBriefly; accents are kept where those lists keep them. Lengths come from the WRC Generations fandom wiki (in-game data) where it covers a rally. For the others they come from WRC 8 (2019) or WRC 9/10 figures for the same stages, which may differ slightly in WRCG. Where both exist, WRC 8 figures are within about 0.1 km of the WRCG wiki for most stages, but the super specials Lousada and Barcelona changed by about 0.2 km. Counts per rally reconcile to the official 165: 109 on the calendar rallies and 56 on the bonus rallies, including one shakedown per rally. The Monte-Carlo snow share is the wiki's figure for snow patches on tarmac.
